meta.name: P-51D Mustang
meta.summary: Single-seat WWII fighter: Packard V-1650-7 Merlin V-12 (two-stage, two-speed supercharger, aftercooler, injection carburetor), Hamilton Standard four-blade constant-speed propeller, ventral radiator scoop, hydraulic landing gear and flaps, 24 V DC electrics. Limits and procedures from the AN 01-60JE-1 pilot's handbook; guns are drawn for layout only. Many are flown today as warbirds — their current flight manual, maintenance manuals and inspection program govern.

components.name: Airframe (fuselage, wing, tail)
components.desc: All-metal semi-monocoque fuselage, laminar-flow wing (span 37 ft / 11.28 m, 5° dihedral), bubble canopy. Overall length 32 ft 3 in (9.83 m), height 12 ft 2 in (3.71 m). Fuselage and wing skins are drawn see-through; Hide guards removes them.
components.src: Pima Air & Space Museum — P-51D specifications; AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Radiator scoop and exit flap
components.desc: Ventral air scoop housing the oil cooler (front) and the combined engine/aftercooler radiator; the exit flap at the rear controls airflow. Normal control is AUTOMATIC; manual OPEN/CLOSE and an emergency release are provided.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Flight controls (ailerons, elevators, rudder, flaps)
components.desc: Cable-operated ailerons, elevators and rudder with trim tabs; hydraulic split flaps. Flap limits: 10° 400, 20° 275, 30° 225, 40° 180, 50° 165 mph IAS.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Cockpit, instruments and controls
components.desc: Engine and flight instruments on the main panel; throttle quadrant (throttle, propeller, mixture) and the supercharger, radiator flap, gear and flap controls on the left; electrical switches on the right.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Packard V-1650-7 Merlin
components.desc: 60° V-12, liquid-cooled, 1,649 cu in, two-stage two-speed supercharger with aftercooler and injection carburetor; 1,490 hp take-off. Take-off and military: 61 in. Hg at 3,000 rpm (5 / 15 min). WEP 67 in. Hg (late airplanes, 5 min). Max continuous 2,700 rpm; max cruise 2,400 rpm; max diving 3,240 rpm.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version); Pima Air & Space Museum — P-51D specifications

components.name: Propeller (Hamilton Standard four-blade)
components.desc: Constant-speed, hydromatic four-blade propeller, 11 ft 2 in (3.40 m) diameter, controlled by the governor. Runaway propeller can exceed 3,600 rpm: throttle back to keep 3,240 rpm and slow to about 140 mph IAS.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Coolant system (radiator, header tank, pumps)
components.desc: Separate pumps, expansion tanks and radiator cores for the engine and the supercharger aftercooler. Coolant Type D (70% water / 30% glycol); Type C below -12 °C. Coolant temperature 100–110 °C desired, 121 °C maximum.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Oil system and oil cooler
components.desc: Oil tank ahead of the firewall, oil cooler at the front of the radiator scoop with its own exit flap. 21 US gal capacity, grade 1120. Oil pressure 70–80 psi desired (min 50, max 105); temperature 70–80 °C desired, 105 °C max.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Fuel system
components.desc: Two self-sealing wing tanks (92 US gal each), an 85 gal fuselage tank aft of the cockpit and two 75 gal drop tanks. Booster pumps in the tanks (10–14 psi), selector valve, strainer, engine-driven pump: 16–18 psi desired at the carburetor (16 min, 19 max). 100/130 grade. Use fuselage fuel first down to about 25 gal; no aerobatics with more than 40 gal in it.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Landing gear
components.desc: Hydraulically retracted main gear (inward into the wing) with 27 in tires and hydraulic brakes, plus a retractable, lockable tail wheel (6° steerable with the stick aft, full-swivel with it forward). Do not extend above 170 mph IAS. Warning light and horn if the throttle is closed with the gear not locked down.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Hydraulic system
components.desc: Engine-driven pump, reservoir on the firewall, selector valves and actuators for gear, gear doors and flaps. Pressure 800–1,100 psi at 2,300 rpm.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Electrical system (24 V DC)
components.desc: 24 V DC with an engine-driven generator and a 34 Ah battery behind the pilot; external power preferred for starting. Ammeter 100 A maximum at 2,300 rpm.
components.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

components.name: Wing guns (layout only)
components.desc: Six .50 caliber machine guns, three in each wing. Shown for layout only.
components.src: Pima Air & Space Museum — P-51D specifications

faults.title: Coolant temperature high
causes: Radiator exit flap not opening (actuator, switch, AUTOMATIC control)
Low coolant or a leak (glycol smell, white vapor)
Long ground running or climbing at low airspeed
Coolant pump or header tank fault
checks: In flight: switch the flap to manual OPEN; if the temperature stays high 20–30 s, pull the emergency release (opens to at least 7 in; cannot be reset in flight)
On the ground: limit taxi and run time, face into wind, open the flap
Check coolant level, mix (Type D 70/30) and leaks at hoses, header tank and pump
Test the flap actuator in manual OPEN and CLOSE
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)
faults.safety: Hot coolant is under pressure — let it cool before opening the header tank.

faults.title: Low oil pressure
faults.msg: Oil pressure below 50 psi within 30 s of start, or below 70 psi running
checks: On start: no 50 psi within 30 s — shut down and investigate
Check oil quantity (21 gal system) and for leaks
Check dilution use (3 min maximum)
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Oil temperature high
causes: Oil cooler blocked or low airflow
checks: Open the oil cooler flap (manual)
Reduce power and increase airspeed
On the ground: inspect the oil cooler core for blockage
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Low fuel pressure
causes: Tank run dry or wrong tank selected
Vapor lock at altitude or in hot weather
checks: Select a tank with fuel and switch the booster pump ON
At altitude, keep booster pumps on
Clean the strainer and check the engine-driven pump relief setting
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Supercharger won't shift to high blower
faults.msg: Power falls off above the shift altitude; amber blower light stays off
causes: Aneroid control fault (fails safe to low blower; amber light goes out)
Electrical fault in the shift circuit
checks: Check the switch is in AUTOMATIC; test with the switch in high on the ground per the handbook
Shift is automatic at about 15,700–19,700 ft airplane altitude (V-1650-7), back down about 1,500 ft lower
Avoid below 2,000 rpm in high blower
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Runaway propeller (overspeed)
causes: Loss of oil pressure to the propeller
checks: Throttle back to hold 3,240 rpm, slow to about 140 mph IAS
Land as soon as practical; inspect governor and propeller
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)
faults.safety: Treat the propeller as live whenever the airplane is near anyone: magnetos can fire with a broken P-lead. Ignition OFF and stay out of the arc when pulling it through.

faults.title: Hard starting or won't start
faults.msg: Engine cranks but won't fire, or fires and dies
causes: Liquid lock in lower cylinders (prop not pulled through)
checks: Pull the propeller through 8 blades before start, ignition OFF
Prime 3–4 s cold, 1 s hot
Use external power where possible
Mixture idle cut-off until it fires, then AUTO RICH/RUN
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)
faults.safety: Treat the propeller as live whenever the airplane is near anyone: magnetos can fire with a broken P-lead. Ignition OFF and stay out of the arc when pulling it through.

faults.title: Rough running after idle / plug fouling
faults.msg: Rough engine or large mag drop after taxi or idle
causes: Long idling at low rpm fouls plugs (rich, cold)
Oil-fouled plugs in the lower bank
checks: Avoid long idling; warm up at 1,300 rpm
Clear with a brief run-up per the handbook before the mag check
If it persists, pull and service the plugs
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version); general warbird and Merlin maintenance practice — the aircraft's own manuals and inspection program govern

faults.title: Low hydraulic pressure
checks: Check reservoir level and look for leaks at actuators and lines
Plan for emergency gear extension
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Gear won't extend or lock down
faults.msg: Red light or horn with the gear selected down
checks: Select DOWN and yaw the airplane to swing the gear out
If still unsafe, pull the fairing door emergency knob and yaw again
If the tail wheel doesn't lock, increase speed or pull a brief positive-g pull-out
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Generator not charging
faults.msg: Ammeter shows no charge or voltage low
causes: Generator, voltage regulator or reverse-current relay fault
checks: Check the generator switch and the ammeter at 2,300 rpm
Reduce electrical load and plan to land
On the ground: test the generator, regulator and relay
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Suction out of range
faults.msg: Suction not 3.75–4.25 in. Hg at 2,300 rpm
causes: Vacuum pump or relief valve fault
Leaking or blocked lines or instrument filters
checks: Cross-check the gyro instruments
Adjust the relief valve; replace filters
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

faults.title: Engine failure
checks: Follow the handbook: keep airspeed, drop external stores, fuel shut-off and battery off
Belly-land unless a long runway is available; flaps about 30° with 20° in reserve
faults.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

io.desc: Manifold pressure (61 in. Hg take-off/military; 67 WEP)
Gear warning horn (throttle closed, gear not down)
Radiator flap switch (AUTOMATIC / OPEN / CLOSE / OFF)

sequence.name: Before starting
sequence.desc: Walkaround, fuel and oil quantities, coolant level, propeller pulled through 8 blades with ignition OFF.

sequence.name: Start
sequence.desc: External power, generator ON, throttle START, prop full increase, booster ON (10–14 psi), prime, ignition BOTH, starter. Mixture to RUN when it fires; 50 psi oil within 30 s.

sequence.name: Warm-up and run-up
sequence.desc: Warm up at 1,300 rpm until oil temperature rises and pressure is steady; run-up checks of magnetos, propeller, blower, hydraulic pressure and suction.

sequence.name: Take-off and climb
sequence.desc: 61 in. Hg, 3,000 rpm (5 min). Gear up; radiator flaps AUTOMATIC; blower shifts to high automatically.

sequence.name: Cruise
sequence.desc: Max cruise 2,400 rpm; min recommended 1,600 rpm (2,000 in high blower). Fuselage tank first down to about 25 gal, then alternate wing tanks.

sequence.name: Landing and shutdown
sequence.desc: Gear below 170 mph IAS, flaps within limits; after landing clear the engine, mixture idle cut-off, switches off.

checks.name: Preflight walkaround
checks.why: Most in-flight problems are visible on the ground.
steps: Coolant, oil and fuel levels; drain sumps
Look for coolant and oil leaks under the cowling and scoop
Tires, brakes, struts and gear doors
Propeller blades for nicks; spinner secure
Control surfaces free; hinges and cables
checks.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version); general warbird and Merlin maintenance practice — the aircraft's own manuals and inspection program govern

checks.name: Run-up
checks.why: Catches ignition, propeller and blower faults before flight.
steps: Magneto check at the handbook rpm; compare drops
Hydraulic 800–1,100 psi and suction 3.75–4.25 at 2,300 rpm
checks.src: AN 01-60JE-1 Pilot's Handbook, P-51D and K (avialogs.com text version)

checks.name: Post-flight
checks.why: Leaks and damage show up while things are hot.
steps: Look for fresh coolant, oil and hydraulic leaks
Note any rough running or overtemperature in the log
checks.src: general warbird and Merlin maintenance practice — the aircraft's own manuals and inspection program govern

reference.name: Engine limits
reference.intro: From the AN 01-60JE-1 power plant chart.

devices.func: Disconnects the generator below battery voltage

defects.name: Corrosion of aluminum structure
defects.looks: White powdery deposits, blistered paint, exfoliation along fastener rows, especially in the scoop, wheel wells and lower fuselage.
isolate: Remove panels and inspect low points where water and coolant collect

causes.fix: Clean, treat and re-protect; fix leaks

defects.name: Coolant leaks at Merlin joints and hoses
defects.looks: Glycol smell, white residue, wet hoses or drips under the scoop.

defects.name: Fatigue cracks at fittings and gear attach points
defects.looks: Hairline cracks at bolt holes and fitting radii; fretting.
